coordinated_entry_system.program_name: Marin County Homeless Coordinated Entry System
coordinated_entry_system.administering_agency: Marin County Health and Human Services - Homelessness and Coordinated Care Division
coordinated_entry_system.description: Countywide system ensuring people experiencing homelessness receive services matched to their housing and support needs. The system prioritizes those with the most acute needs and connects them to appropriate interventions including emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, and permanent supportive housing. HUD-funded projects contract with nonprofit agencies as subrecipients to carry out activities.

eligibility_requirements.housing_status: Literally homeless, imminent risk of homelessness, or fleeing domestic violence (HEARTH Act categories 1, 2, and 4)
eligibility_requirements.geographic: Marin County resident or homeless in Marin

resident_input_opportunities: Community input sessions on CoC funding priorities
coordinated_entry_system.leverage_point: Residents can participate in Continuum of Care public meetings where funding priorities are set. The CoC holds annual planning sessions where community input shapes program direction. Contact the Coordinated Entry line to provide feedback or volunteer for Point-in-Time Count.

contact.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM - 4:30 PM (individuals), 9 AM - 5 PM daily (families)

homeward_bound_emergency_shelter.description: Provides emergency shelter and housing-focused services through multiple facilities including Jonathan's Place (38 beds in San Rafael) and New Beginnings Center (80 beds in Novato). Shelters offer counseling, case management, meals, job search assistance, and connections to community resources. The program participates in the Coordinated Entry System to prioritize those with acute needs.
eligible_activities: Veteran-specific services at New Beginnings (VA office onsite)
resident_input_opportunities: Homeward Bound volunteer and donation programs
homeward_bound_emergency_shelter.leverage_point: Community members can support shelter operations through volunteering and donations. Residents can provide feedback on services to case managers. Homeward Bound hosts community events and welcomes input on program improvements.

homeward_bound_permanent_supportive_hous.description: Offers over 350 beds of permanent supportive housing for formerly homeless individuals, including single-room occupancy units, studio apartments, and transitional housing. Residents pay affordable rents and receive ongoing support services. Properties include La Casa Buena (18 studios in Corte Madera), Jonathan's Place Housing (16 units in San Rafael), King Street Senior Housing (12 rooms in Larkspur), Fourth Street Center (20 units in San Rafael), and Next Key Apartments (29 transitional studios in Novato).

eligibility_requirements.housing_status: Formerly homeless, typically chronic homeless or high acuity

homeward_bound_permanent_supportive_hous.leverage_point: Residents of supportive housing can participate in site-based resident councils. Community members can support the program through donations and advocacy for affordable housing development.

care_teams_homeless_outreach.program_name: CARE Teams - Community Alternative Response & Engagement
care_teams_homeless_outreach.description: Mobile outreach teams staffed by trained Peer Outreach Specialists, including people with lived experience of homelessness, mental illness, substance abuse, or incarceration. Teams provide immediate assistance like wellness checks, food, clothing, and sleeping bags, build trust relationships over time, and connect clients to mental health services, housing programs, and permanent housing. Often the first point of contact for people experiencing homelessness.
eligible_activities: Basic needs provision (food, clothing, sleeping bags)
Transportation to shelters, hospitals, or detox

eligibility_requirements.geographic: Marin County (CARE Team One covers West Marin specifically)

care_teams_homeless_outreach.leverage_point: Community members can report homeless encampments or individuals needing assistance to CARE Teams. The program welcomes donations and volunteers. Input on outreach priorities can be provided through Community Action Marin.

coverage_areas.care_team_one: West Marin (Pt. Reyes, Tomales, Inverness, Stinson Beach, Bolinas)

odyssey_team_mental_health.program_name: Odyssey Team - Homeless Outreach Full Service Partnership
odyssey_team_mental_health.administering_agency: Marin County Health and Human Services - Behavioral Health & Recovery Services
odyssey_team_mental_health.description: Provides a comprehensive, integrated continuum of services to individuals who are seriously and persistently mentally ill and who are homeless. Services are guided by principles of recovery and consumer empowerment. While not a housing program, Odyssey supports clients to become self-sufficient in their housing goals through intensive case management and mental health treatment.
odyssey_team_mental_health.leverage_point: Community members can attend Mental Health Advisory Board meetings where program priorities are discussed. Anyone can make a referral into the Odyssey Program. Input on behavioral health services can be provided through BHRS community meetings.

contact.referral: Anyone can make a referral into the Odyssey Program

ritter_center_services.description: Prevents and resolves homelessness while improving health and dignity for people living in poverty in Marin County. Provides integrated support including primary medical care, behavioral health counseling, substance abuse treatment, dental care, rental assistance, case management, and operates the largest food pantry in Marin County (22,000+ grocery bags weekly to 375+ households).

eligibility_requirements.housing_status: Experiencing or at risk of homelessness

ritter_center_services.leverage_point: Clients can provide feedback through patient portals and case managers. Community members can support through donations and volunteering. Ritter Center welcomes input on community needs through various programs.

rapid_rehousing.administering_agency: Multiple agencies (Ritter Center, Community Action Marin, St. Vincent de Paul, Adopt A Family)
rapid_rehousing.description: Short-term rental assistance and supportive services lasting from a deposit to up to two years. Best suited for individuals and families who need support to get back on their feet after homelessness. Helps find new housing and provides short-term support once housed, including case management, financial assistance for rent and move-in costs, and connections to community resources.

eligibility_requirements.self_sufficiency: Expected to become self-sufficient when program ends (no income requirement to enter)

resident_input_opportunities: CoC public hearings on funding priorities
rapid_rehousing.leverage_point: Residents can provide input on rapid rehousing program design through CoC public meetings. Individual feedback to case managers helps improve services. Community can advocate for increased rapid rehousing funding.

st_vincent_de_paul_services.program_name: St. Vincent de Paul Society of Marin County
st_vincent_de_paul_services.administering_agency: St. Vincent de Paul Society of Marin County
st_vincent_de_paul_services.description: Provides direct services to people experiencing homelessness and poverty since 1946. Operates a free dining room serving 200,000 warm meals annually, a Housing Help Desk for crisis assistance and case management, and a Housing Outreach Team. Offers rapid rehousing assistance and crisis assistance to prevent evictions through early intervention.

eligibility_requirements.housing_status: Homeless or at risk of homelessness

st_vincent_de_paul_services.leverage_point: Community members can volunteer through parish networks or donate directly. Clients can provide feedback on services at the dining room and help desk. The organization relies heavily on community involvement.

safe_team_san_rafael.program_name: SAFE Team - Specialized Assistance For Everyone
safe_team_san_rafael.administering_agency: City of San Rafael (operated by Petaluma People Services Center)
safe_team_san_rafael.description: Mobile mental health crisis response team launched March 2023 as an alternative to police response for mental health crises. Responds to people under the influence of drugs or alcohol, in need of mental health treatment, or who need shelter. Provides counseling and transportation to appropriately staffed locations rather than jail or emergency rooms.

eligibility_requirements.crisis_type: Mental health or substance use crisis

safe_team_san_rafael.leverage_point: San Rafael residents can provide input on SAFE Team operations through City Council meetings and public comment periods. Community feedback on mental health crisis response helps shape program priorities.

contact.dispatch: Through San Rafael Police dispatch for appropriate calls

income_limits_2025.note: Income limits published by HUD. Most homelessness programs serve extremely low income (30% AMI) but may extend to very low income (50% AMI) for prevention services.

211_marin.note: General information and referral for all social services

marin_county_hhs_homelessness.note: County Homelessness and Coordinated Care Division
